geological_process: Chronostratigraphic boundary; end-Permian mass extinction interval
description: Formal base of the Triassic. The Indian Plate is part of Gondwana at this time.
uncertainty_notes: Boundary age is revised periodically by the ICS.

description: Formal base of the Cretaceous in the ICS chart used here (v2024/12).
uncertainty_notes: The base of the Cretaceous has been dated differently in earlier charts.

event_name: Break-up of Gondwana: Indian Plate separates from Antarctica and Australia
description: India, as part of eastern Gondwana, separates from Antarctica and Australia and begins moving northwards. Published reconstructions place the separation in the Early Cretaceous.
uncertainty_notes: Reconstructions disagree on the timing of separation by several million years and on the exact margins involved.

description: Volcanism along the Madagascar margin is dated to about 88 Ma and is associated with the separation of Madagascar from India.
uncertainty_notes: The date refers to volcanic rocks, not to a single moment of separation.

event_name: Rapid northward motion of the Indian Plate
description: The Indian Plate moves northward across the ocean between Gondwana and Eurasia at plate speeds that are high compared with most plates. The speeds implied by the model used here are computed in the dataset, not quoted from the literature.
uncertainty_notes: Speeds depend on the rotation model and on the choice of reference frame.

description: U-Pb dating places the main phase of Deccan volcanism around the Cretaceous-Paleogene boundary. The Deccan lavas underlie much of the modern Deccan Plateau.
uncertainty_notes: Volcanism began earlier and continued later at lower intensity; the range given is the main phase only.

geological_process: Chronostratigraphic boundary; end of the Mesozoic; end-Cretaceous mass extinction
description: Formal end of the Cretaceous and of the age of non-avian dinosaurs.
uncertainty_notes: Radioisotopic dating of the boundary event is consistent with the ICS value to within about 0.05 Ma.

description: Published estimates for the onset of collision range from the latest Cretaceous to the late Eocene. Recent syntheses favour initial contact around 60 to 50 Ma, with a two-stage model placing final continental collision later.
uncertainty_notes: No single agreed date exists. Estimates differ by up to about 30 Myr depending on the criterion (first sediment mixing, ophiolite obduction, palaeomagnetic convergence, or cessation of marine sedimentation).

event_name: Crustal shortening and mountain building in the Himalaya
geological_process: Crustal shortening, thrusting, metamorphism and erosion
description: Following collision, convergence is accommodated by shortening and thickening of the Indian margin crust and uplift of the Himalayan-Tibetan system, continuing today.
uncertainty_notes: The timing of uplift of individual ranges and of the Tibetan Plateau is debated.

description: Formal boundary between the Eocene and the Oligocene.

event_name: Two-stage collision model: closure of the Greater India Basin
description: One published model proposes an initial India-Asia contact near 50 Ma and the closure of a Greater India Basin, and hence full continental collision, around 25 to 20 Ma.
confidence: low to medium: one of several competing models
uncertainty_notes: The existence and size of a Greater India Basin is contested.

description: Formal base of the Pleistocene and of the Quaternary.
Formal base of the Holocene (about 11,700 years ago). Sea level and ice-sheet change in the late Pleistocene and Holocene are not modelled in this application.
